questions.q: What is the core difference between classic and generative orchestration?
options: Classic orchestration is only available on mobile devices

Classic orchestration matches a user's message to pre-authored trigger phrases for one topic; generative orchestration reasons over descriptions and can dynamically select and chain multiple tools, topics, or knowledge sources
Generative orchestration requires every possible user phrasing to be predicted in advance, while classic orchestration does not
There is no functional difference between the two modes
questions.explain: Classic orchestration is closer to fixed-path thinking: a user's message is matched against trigger phrases. Generative orchestration reasons about descriptions and can dynamically choose and sequence multiple components.

questions.q: When generative orchestration decides which tool to call, which signal carries the most weight?
options: The tool's description
The alphabetical order in which tools were added
The color of the tool's icon
The number of times the tool has been tested
questions.explain: The description is the most important factor the orchestrator uses to match a user's intent to the right tool, topic, or knowledge source — which is why writing a clear, jargon-free one matters.

questions.q: In the real activity-map example from this lesson (a weather tool), what did the agent do automatically when the user asked about the weather in Seattle?
options: It rejected the question because no tool was configured
It filled the tool's Location input with "Seattle" from the user's message, then generated a clarifying question for the missing units value
It emailed an administrator to approve the request before responding
It ignored the location mentioned and asked the user to type it again
questions.explain: The agent recognized "Seattle" from the conversation and pre-filled the tool's input automatically, then generated its own follow-up question for the measurement-units input it still needed.

questions.q: Why does the lesson warn against a tool description like "Gets EPS for any stock ticker"?
options: Because stock-related tools are not allowed in Copilot Studio
Because it's too long for the description field
Because it relies on jargon ("EPS") instead of plainly stating what the tool does, making it harder for the orchestrator to match it to a plainly worded user question
Because descriptions are ignored by generative orchestration entirely
questions.explain: Jargon-heavy descriptions make it harder for the orchestrator to match a tool to how real users phrase their questions. Clear, specific, non-jargon descriptions improve tool selection accuracy.

questions.q: What does the End all topics node do?
options: It permanently deletes every topic in the agent
It cancels any remaining steps the orchestrator had planned, stopping the conversation early
It publishes the agent to all configured channels at once
It clears the agent's knowledge sources
questions.explain: End all topics cancels any remaining planned steps the orchestrator intended to run, which is useful when a conversation needs to stop early rather than continuing through a multi-step plan.
